# Storage Shape Audit Results

Generated from the review-storage audit strategy in
`REVIEW_STORAGE_SHAPE_AUDIT_PLAN.md`.

## Durable Audit Control Framework

This is the audit control plane. Later stories must resume here and append
normalized evidence rather than creating parallel result files. Narrative
findings retained later in this file are discovery input, not substitutes for
the manifests and proof records below.

### Certification Snapshot

| Field | Value | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `overallCertification` | `INCOMPLETE` | The API manifest has 67 nonterminal rows and one blocked row, the UI/runtime manifest has 49 nonterminal rows, and the background/operator manifest has two nonterminal consumers. US-016 through US-022 trace the LLM, Human, Both, Unassessed, detail, prompt-preview, global full-text, admin-support, warning, health, runtime-readiness, durable progress, token-prefix/substring search, select-all, and add-to-project source surfaces, but search ownership, filter/count/snapshot parity, substring execution, claim/progress/lifecycle authority, and browser/desktop runtime parity remain unresolved. The US-003 through US-014 source censuses and nine blocked US-015 physical-measurement rows also remain nonterminal or blocked; no inherited recommendation is actionable. |
| Framework version | `US-001 / 2026-07-21` | First normalized, resumable evidence structure. |
| Latest normalized story | `US-022 / 2026-07-21` | Source-only tracing separates submitted all-token prefix list search, the internal token-prefix contract, unwired async substring jobs, cumulative loaded-row selection, select-all criteria, explicit-ID selection, keyset worker batches, and actual project writes; adds four API/read rows, four UI/runtime rows, one background row, and five preliminary maps. Filter signatures, ordering, latest-snapshot semantics, keyset batching, ID/payload caps, progress, owners, tests, Eden/shared-client/browser-proxy/desktop paths, and consumed/ignored fields are recorded without starting a runtime or opening live DuckDB. Product authority, substring execution, count/filter/snapshot parity, claim/progress/lifecycle proof, physical budgets, exact missing tests, and runtime parity remain blockers. |
| Durable result file | `STORAGE_SHAPE_AUDIT_PLAN.md` | The only audit-result artifact; Ralph may separately update tracker metadata. |

`overallCertification: PASS` is forbidden until every in-scope manifest row is
`classified`, every reconciliation has zero nonterminal and blocked rows, all
completion gates pass, and every actionable recommendation has all applicable
positive and negative proof checks satisfied. Otherwise it remains
`INCOMPLETE`.

### Scope And Mutation Boundary

- Audit work may read repository files and approved immutable snapshots. It
  must not change repository schemas, code, routes, projectors, retention,
  runtime behavior, or data.
- Durable audit results go only in this file. Changes under `.ralph-tui/` are
  tracker metadata, not audit evidence.
- Never open or query the live DuckDB file directly. Physical evidence is
  acceptable only from approved snapshot tooling or an explicitly approved,
  isolated disposable fixture in a story that authorizes it.
- Do not start a server, worker, projector, migration, maintenance command, or
  database writer merely to fill this framework.
- Model, provider, thinking level, prompt set, content flags, memory limit, and
  runtime profile are benchmark-critical. Preserve failures under those
  settings; do not retry, downgrade, or silently work around them.

### Inherited Evidence And Disposition Rule

The pre-US-001 content below is preserved because it contains useful
repo-derived observations. Its factual claims remain discovery leads subject to
exact citation and manifest reconciliation. Every inherited `Disposition:`,
deletion/move candidate, target shape, implementation slice, and current
recommendation is **provisional** with
`recommendationActionability: unresolved` unless a later normalized row
cross-references revised proof.

- A broad path or glob is a discovery source, not a proof citation.
- A test, fixture, plan, comment, generated file, or historical migration does
  not prove production use.
- Absence from literal search does not prove absence from generated SQL,
  aliases, registries, allowlists, scripts, or runtime paths.
- No move, derive, archive, or delete recommendation may become stronger before
  API, writer, lifecycle, recovery, export, transfer, and retention evidence is
  traced. Final actionability also requires all applicable proof domains below.

## Stable Row IDs And Cross-References

Every normalized row receives an opaque stable ID. IDs identify evidence
records, not mutable object names.

| Prefix | Row family |
| --- | --- |
| `API-####` | Mounted API and read-contract manifest |
| `UIR-####` | UI and runtime consumption manifest |
| `BGO-####` | Background and operator surface manifest |
| `DBO-####` | DuckDB object, temporary shape, payload, or generated-file manifest |
| `CMF-####` | Column and material field manifest |
| `MAP-####` | Route-to-query and route-to-table map |
| `LIN-####` | Column-level lineage |
| `TLI-####` | Table, index, and lifecycle inventory |
| `FAN-####` | Fan-out or duplicate-byte measurement |
| `DSP-####` | Storage disposition |
| `PRF-####` | Positive or negative proof check |
| `TGT-####` | Candidate target shape |
| `SLC-####` | Implementation slice and benchmark gate |
| `EVD-####` | Exact evidence citation |
| `CMD-####` | Command or explicitly skipped check |
| `BLK-####` | Audit blocker |
| `OQ-####` | Owner question |

ID rules:

1. Allocate the next decimal ID within its family and zero-pad to four digits.
2. Never renumber, reuse, or derive an ID from a route, symbol, table, or
   column name.
3. A rename keeps the ID and records both locators. A split creates new IDs and
   cross-references the originating ID.
4. Keep retired or superseded rows for history; record an evidence-backed
   terminal state instead of deleting them.
5. Use IDs for all cross-output links. Citations supplement IDs but never
   replace them.

## State Model

The four state fields answer different questions and must never substitute for
one another.

### Manifest `auditStatus`

Only these values are valid:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `not-started` | Discovered and allocated, but no required lineage has been traced. |
| `traced-to-api` | Product/API or explicit non-route scope is known; writer and lifecycle proof is incomplete. |
| `traced-to-writer` | Producers and mutations are traced; lifecycle/recovery or other required evidence is incomplete. |
| `traced-to-lifecycle` | Invalidation, replay/recovery, retention, and cleanup are traced; measurement or classification is incomplete. |
| `measured` | Required approved physical evidence is recorded; classification is incomplete. |
| `classified` | The in-scope row has complete required evidence and a use classification; this does not make a recommendation actionable. |
| `blocked` | Reconciliation-terminal for counting, but required evidence cannot currently be obtained; any blocked row prevents `PASS`. |
| `out-of-scope` | Evidence proves the row is outside the project-review domain and records the exact reason. |

The nonterminal values are `not-started`, `traced-to-api`,
`traced-to-writer`, `traced-to-lifecycle`, and `measured`. Every row with
one of those values must contain concrete `missingEvidence` and at least one
`ownerQuestionIds` reference. A `blocked` row must contain both as well.
`classified` and `out-of-scope` are the evidence-complete terminal states;
`out-of-scope` additionally requires a cited scope reason.

### `proofCheckState`

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `satisfied` | The named positive or negative proof is present and exactly cited. |
| `pending` | The proof is required but has not been established. |
| `blocked` | The proof is required and an identified blocker prevents collection. |
| `not-applicable` | Cited scope evidence shows why this proof domain cannot apply. |

### `recommendationActionability`

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `actionable` | Every applicable proof check and benchmark gate is satisfied. |
| `unresolved` | One or more proof checks or design consequences remain pending. |
| `blocked` | A required proof check is blocked. |

### `overallCertification`

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `PASS` | All manifests reconcile with no blocked rows, every completion gate passes, and every actionable recommendation has complete proof. |
| `INCOMPLETE` | Any other condition, including an empty/unbaselined manifest, nonterminal row, blocker, pending gate, or unresolved required proof. |

## Exact Evidence And Source Classification

Each `EVD-####` record states the claim it supports, source class, exact
locator, and `CMD-####` or approved snapshot that exposed it. Accepted exact
locators include:

- repository file plus symbol, exported constant, test name, or exact SQL
  statement shape;
- mounted method and route, UI query key, worker/scheduler entry point, or
  operator command;
- fully qualified table, column, JSON key, constraint, index name/expression,
  or temporary-table naming shape;
- exact current/final migration and every forward migration that changes it;
- immutable approved snapshot identity plus collection command and fixed
  benchmark configuration; and
- exact local path scheme or export/transfer mapping plus producer and consumer.

Every evidence record uses one source class:

| Source class | Evidentiary use |
| --- | --- |
| `production` | Runtime route, client, service, writer, worker, projector, lifecycle, recovery, export, transfer, or operator code. |
| `test` | Test behavior only; corroborates but does not prove production use. |
| `fixture` | Seed/mock/disposable-fixture behavior only; never live physical evidence. |
| `plan` | Intended or historical design only. |
| `comment` | Discovery hint only. |
| `generated` | Generated types/files; record the source and do not infer runtime mounting. |
| `historical-migration` | Schema history only; reconcile current declarations and forward migrations. |
| `approved-snapshot` | Immutable approved non-live physical evidence with fixed configuration. |

Globs, directory-level citations, unrecorded searches, and bare claims such as
“the tests cover this” cannot satisfy proof. Conflicting evidence is preserved
and linked to a blocker or owner question, never resolved by assumption.

### Registry And Parity Discrepancies

| Discrepancy | Exact result | Audit consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Declared mount versus product composition | The 16 `mounted:true` read-inventory entries minus `routeSurfaceRoutes` is exactly `POST /api/projectsreviewshealth`; `ProjectsRoutes.ts#projectsRoutes` confirms the handler is not composed. | `API-0017` is `blocked`; parity evidence cannot establish reachability. |
| Parity union versus read-contract inventory | The 18-entry route/job parity union minus the declared-mounted read inventory is exactly `POST /api/projects/add_articles_by_ids` and `GET /api/articles/pdf-fetch-jobs/:jobId`. | `API-0018` and `API-0019` remain `traced-to-api` pending registry ownership. |
| Adjacent mounted flow closures | Add-job status, export-job status/download, and prompt export are in `routeSurfaceRoutes` but absent from both review-serving registries. | `API-0020` through `API-0023` prevent a claim that the review read registry is exhaustive. |
| Add-by-filter semantic mapping | Route inventory maps `review.bulk.substringSelection`; production creates `review.bulk.selection` and selects `none` or `tokenPrefix` search mode. | Contract parity for `API-0012` needs owner resolution; no value was silently substituted. |

### Read-Contract Matrix

This matrix is the exact `reviewServingReadContractList` baseline. Budget cells
are `maxPageSize / maxResultRows / maxEstimatedResultBytes / timeoutMs /
allowsTempSpill`. Every contract has a 5,000 ms timeout and forbids temp spill.
These are per-reader admission budgets, not aggregate HTTP-response budgets.

| Contract key | Allowed filters | Named exact counts | Order and cursor | Freshness, search, access | Budget |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `review.llm.rows` | `duplicateFlag`, `importRoute`, `publicationYear`, `articleCreatedAtFrom`, `articleCreatedAtTo`, `searchTokenPrefix`, `conflictFlag`, `llmHasJudgment`, `llmStatus`, `promptAnswer` | `review.list.total`, `review.list.filteredTotal`, `review.llm.assessedByPrompt` | `sort_key DESC, article_id ASC`; same cursor | ready snapshot; token prefix; ordered prefix | `501 / 501 / 2000000 / 5000 / false` |

### Exactness, Pagination, Freshness, And Failure Semantics

| Concern | Frozen current behavior | Evidence IDs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List exactness and pagination | LLM, Human, Both, and Unassessed select snapshot-scoped candidates in contract order, fetch `limit + 1`, return at most `limit`, and derive `nextCursor` from the last returned row. There is no offset selection. LLM echoes normalized body `page`; Human/Both/Unassessed report page 1 until a cursor is supplied, then echo normalized `page`. | `EVD-0003`, `EVD-0005`, `EVD-0009` |
| Count exactness | Unfiltered counts read named summary rows. Dynamic filters execute exact `COUNT(DISTINCT serving.article_id)` over the same project, config hash, snapshot, list mode, date/status/posting/search/queue predicates. Counts are not approximate. The count-only HTTP route converts all failures to zero plus `error`; list routes throw count failures. | `EVD-0004`, `EVD-0009` |
| Filter exactness | Review facets use four named facet definitions; Human facets use two. Options are identity-scoped and bounded to 512. Rejected facet/option reads become empty arrays; a wholly missing manifest returns empty arrays and `searchScope.availability:"unavailable"`. | `EVD-0003`, `EVD-0010` |
| Snapshot selection | List and filter services request the active manifest for the exact review-config hash, otherwise the last-known-good manifest, and pass its snapshot and component identities to every reader. Bulk jobs persist latest or explicit pinned semantics; export pins may include expiry. | `EVD-0005`, `EVD-0009`, `EVD-0012` |
| `requireReadySnapshot` behavior | Admission accepts `ready`; it also accepts `stale` only when the caller explicitly passes `allowStale:true`. Current list/filter services do pass that flag after selecting last-known-good. Candidate is `indexing`; failed or missing is `unavailable`; those states reject foreground reads. The behavior name therefore does not mean stale is impossible. | `EVD-0004`, `EVD-0005`, `EVD-0009` |
| `allowStaleSnapshot` behavior | Health/warning contracts do not reject on freshness alone, but the reader still requires a resolvable project manifest. Warning treats active and retired manifests as usable and exposes readable/usable/status diagnostics. Health has equivalent source behavior but is not mounted. | `EVD-0005`, `EVD-0011` |
| Search unavailable behavior | Synchronous substring search is rejected. Token-prefix search requires `searchState.ready` bound to the same snapshot. Substring contracts represent asynchronous job criteria/state. | `EVD-0004`, `EVD-0005` |
| Cursor validity | A cursor is versioned and rejected on malformed schema, contract, filter signature, review-config hash, snapshot, component base generation, patch watermark, projection identity, sort direction/key, or sort arity mismatch. | `EVD-0005`, `EVD-0006` |
| Existing retry behavior | Human/Both/Unassessed date and reader data statements retry only the message containing `An unknown error occurred in Effect.tryPromise`, with at most four underlying attempts and delays of 100, 250, and 500 ms. Their dynamic count path calls the same helper around the already-retrying database, permitting four outer groups of up to four underlying attempts (16 total) if the matching error persists. No retry/fallback was added by this audit; benchmark evidence must disclose the layered behavior. | `EVD-0009`, `EVD-0166` |
| Response-budget tiers | Per-reader contracts enforce the matrix above. Synthetic route-parity cases separately cap direct reader latency at 1,000 ms and result/current-behavior bytes at 50,000. The Phase-6 workload separately caps global p95 at 2,000 ms and p99 at 5,000 ms. None is evidence of full serialized HTTP response size unless the later route benchmark measures that boundary. | `EVD-0003`, `EVD-0007`, `EVD-0013` |

### Benchmark-Critical Configuration Freeze

A value marked `pending` is not permission to choose a convenient value. The
first approved physical run must supply it once and later comparisons must use
the same recorded identity. Repository defaults are evidence about resolution
logic, not approval of a benchmark value.

| Configuration dimension | Frozen value or exact absence | proofCheckState | Missing evidence / owner question |

The audit shell had no override; empty-environment runtime defaults resolve `SERVER_ROLE=auto` to `6400MiB` on this macOS host. The smoke report instead records `not-set-synthetic-validation`. None is adopted as the physical benchmark value. | `pending` | Approve one explicit release value; `OQ-0005`. |

Existing route-specific retry and last-known-good behavior is frozen in the semantics table and must be visible in results. | `satisfied` | Product approval of the existing retry/count-error behavior remains `OQ-0008`. |

### Timing Boundaries

No current physical timing is claimed. Future evidence must emit these as
separate fields; summing or overlapping them without raw timestamps is invalid.

| Timing field | Start | Stop | Included | Explicitly excluded | Current evidence state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sourceSeedOrImportMs` | Fixture generator/import begins writing authoritative source rows. | Final source transaction/checkpoint required by the fixture commits. | Source generation, parsing, and authoritative writes. | Projector/rebuild queue wait or work; route reads. | Definition fixed; value `pending`. |
| `projectionOrRebuildMs` | Rebuild request is durably accepted or the first projection work item starts; record both timestamps when queue wait exists. | Required components publish the active snapshot and manifest identities used by reads. | Queue wait as a separate subfield, projection/rebuild work, publication. | Source import/seeding; foreground route reads. | Definition fixed; value `pending`. |
| `foregroundRouteReadMs` | After request parsing, immediately before route admission/current-behavior read; later reports must also record end-to-end HTTP time separately. | Reader result and required bounded hydration/count work complete; serialized HTTP completion is a separate measurement. | Admission, snapshot/diagnostic reads, candidate query, bounded hydration/count work, and disclosed retries. | Source seeding/import, projection/rebuild, async job execution. | Per-reader synthetic timing exists; physical and HTTP values `pending`. |

The current smoke harness accepts `latencyMs` observations embedded in its
work items and does not time source seeding or projection. Its release report
therefore cannot satisfy these three physical timing fields. Phase-6 scope tags
named `import`, `dirtyMaterialization`, and `servingRefresh` do not change that.

### Metric Definitions And Budgets

| Metric | Exact current definition | Gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Latency percentiles | Nearest-rank over all sample `latencyMs` values: sort ascending and choose `ceil(n*p)-1`; empty set is 0. Per-operation p95/p99 use the same function. | Global p95 <= 2,000 ms; p99 <= 5,000 ms. |
| Memory | `startRssBytes` and `endRssBytes` sample `process.memoryUsage().rss`; `peakRssBytes` is the maximum of start, end, and sample RSS. Growth is end minus start in validation. | Peak <= 20 GiB; growth <= 4 GiB. |
| Queue depth | Average of sample queue depths rounded to two decimals; peak is maximum, empty set 0. | Recorded; workload-shape validation requires nonnegative values. |
| Rows | `rowsReturned` and `rowsScanned` are sums across samples; each operation also enforces its declared page and max-scanned rows. | No returned row above operation page; no scanned row above operation cap. |
| Temp usage | Peak and total of sample `tempUsageBytes`; release context separately records `tempDirGrowthBytes`. | Every accepted foreground sample must be zero spill; growth must be nonnegative. |
| Work | Counts admitted, rejected, and total samples from admission results. | Recorded and validated; benchmark-critical failures remain failures. |
| Response bytes | Contract `maxEstimatedResultBytes` is admission metadata; parity uses UTF-8 byte length of JSON reader rows with a 50,000-byte synthetic cap. | Later HTTP evidence must separately measure serialized route bytes against an owner-approved route budget. |

| Direct DuckDB CLI, direct live-file open, server/projector/migration/maintenance commands | None for US-002. | Explicitly prohibited. |

## US-004 Prompt, Model, And Review-Configuration Census

This census continues the US-003 lexical migration-chain method and uses only
checked-in migrations, production source, and tests. No live DuckDB was opened
or queried and no runtime was started. One focused verification suite applied
the checked-in migrations to its auto-cleaned isolated temporary database; that
non-production fixture corroborates tests only and supplies no census or
physical evidence. Physical fields already enumerated by US-003 are
cross-referenced rather than duplicated. Every disposition remains
`unresolved`; no recommendation, repository schema, route, projector, retention
policy, runtime behavior, or persistent data is changed.

### Preserved Cross-Contract Gaps

These are source observations, not proposed fixes or dispositions.

| Gap | Exact observation | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Legacy prompt hash | New immutable prompt identity covers original/transformed/heading/type, but review-config fallback for a null `content_hash` hashes only `original_text`. | Legacy transformed text, heading, or type changes can be invisible to that fallback; authoritative compatibility policy is missing. |
| Prompt criteria metadata | `criteria_disposition`, `criteria_section_key`, and `criteria_section_label` feed payload/summary/comparison/export behavior. They are absent from prompt/review hash inputs and both invalidation field unions. | Configuration can affect review interpretation without an enumerated review-identity/invalidation dimension. |
| Prompt state applicability | Review-config/projector reads require enabled and both link/prompt not archived. Queue/live-prompt and judgment-visibility paths do not all apply the same three predicates. | Reachability and reuse can differ by caller for the same stored configuration. |
| Scope/date applicability | Projector scope applies inclusive dates; stored-judgment affected-project lookup matches archived/model/flags and scope membership but does not apply dates or prompt/link archival. | A judgment delta can target a different project set than a scope rebuild. |
| Model/provider execution | Review hash includes provider connection/kind/base URL, model remote ID/variant, and only `metadata_json.$.options`; judgment natural key uses model UUID plus flags. Execution snapshots include materially more provider/model/config state. | In-place execution-setting changes can invalidate review state while matching the prior judgment key. |
| Route-only constraints | API validation rejects inverted dates and simultaneous full-text modes; DuckDB has no corresponding `CHECK`, and transfer/import writers are separate paths. | Static schema alone cannot certify persisted values satisfy route rules. |

All six gaps remain under `BLK-0011`; no resolver default, migration proposal,
or assumed authoritative contract is introduced.

## US-005 Judgment, Human-Review, And Review-State Census

This story inventories durable review truth and the judgment-completion handoff
that writes it. It includes the canonical DuckDB objects, the per-job SQLite
`judgment_outbox`, the judge-worker SQLite `completion_outbox` and
`pending_token_use`, the implicit SQLite AUTOINCREMENT catalog entry, and both
file containers. Job admission, queue, lease, heartbeat, accepted-claim,
completion-ack, retry/control, and request-attempt closeout tables remain owned
by US-006. `app.review_source_change_outbox` and the review/import delta family
remain owned by US-007. This boundary prevents duplicate manifest rows while
still tracing every US-005 producer and consumer.

The declared DuckDB shape is derived from the complete full-file-name lexical
migration chain. The two SQLite shapes are derived from their base `CREATE`
statements plus every current runtime schema upgrader, rebuild, index creator,
and implicit AUTOINCREMENT object. Neither derivation proves the shape of a
deployed file. No DuckDB or SQLite data file was opened for the census.

All storage dispositions added by US-005 are `unresolved`.
`recommendationActionability` remains `unresolved`,
`overallCertification` remains `INCOMPLETE`, and no `DSP-####`, `TGT-####`, or
`SLC-####` row is created or changed.

and SQLite autoindexes are not double-counted as named application indexes.

### Model, Content-Setting, Sequence, And Snapshot Identity

| Contract/object | Exact identity dimensions | Source-observed consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Active direct LLM judgment reuse | `article_id`, `prompt_id`, `model_id`, `use_title`, `use_abstract`, `use_fulltext`, `use_fulltext_no_images`, plus `deleted_at IS NULL` | Model and all four content flags participate. `project_id`, snapshot project/name, chunking, answers, and timestamps do not. |
| Physical judgment uniqueness and index | Same seven model/content dimensions plus `delete_generation`; no `deleted_at` predicate | A soft-deleted generation still occupies its physical key. Two delete paths leave generation unchanged while one advances it; importer lookup fixes generation at zero (`BLK-0012`). |
| Per-job completion truth | `judgment_id` and unique `queue_prompt_id`; global outbox order `(job_id,outbox_seq)`; payload repeats model ID and all four flags | `outbox_seq` is monotonic only within one SQLite file and is bridged into DuckDB by the compound marker PK. No continuity/gap invariant is declared. |
| Worker completion truth | `claim_id` PK; payload binds job/queue/article/prompt/model, execution-snapshot ID/hash, and all four flags | One unacked completion is updated per claim; no SQL constraint verifies payload identity against relational columns. |
| Token-use truth | UUID `id`; optional `judgment_job_id`; request attempts use `requestAttemptId` + `providerKey` and durable-closeout references | `sglang_model`/`modelName` is not a model FK or the judgment's `model_id`; all content flags appear only when token evidence is nested in a completion payload. |
| Execution snapshot | UUID `id`; unique `(job_id,queue_record_id,claim_id)`; relational model ID + four flags; SHA-256 over the complete stable version-2 payload | Payload additionally freezes project dates/name, selected import, article/prompt, provider, model metadata/options, and content. On conflict, current code reads the old row rather than comparing a newly built hash. 0083 can leave relational and embedded model identities divergent (`BLK-0013`). |
| Human prompt/summary/review/assessment | Human prompt unique `(project_id,article_id,prompt_id)`; summary/review unique `(project_id,article_id)`; assessment unique `judgment_id` | LLM model/content flags are not dimensions of these human/manual identities. Null human project identity, review writer ownership, and assessment creation ownership remain unresolved. |

### Current-Schema Drift Preserved As Blockers

1. `app.judgment` has three source-observed notions of current identity:
   active `deleted_at IS NULL`, physical `delete_generation`, and importer
   `delete_generation = 0`. Delete paths mutate them differently. No one is
   promoted to authoritative (`BLK-0012`).
2. Migration 0083 remaps `judgment_execution_snapshot.model_id` without
   rewriting `payload_json.identity.modelId`, `payload_json.model.id`, model or
   provider payload, or `payload_hash`; conflict readback also does not compare
   the newly derived hash (`BLK-0013`).
3. `judgment_human.project_id` is nullable while its natural unique key and
   former lookup index are project-first. Null-distinct uniqueness, null-safe
   readers, and the missing rebuilt index are recorded without inventing the
   intended null-project cardinality (`BLK-0014`).
4. Local SQLite schemas have no checked-in ordered migration ledger. Current
   code upgrades only named subsets, can rebuild/synthesize pending-token
   identity, adds `local_applied_at` outside the base create, and repairs legacy
   evidence on open. No deployed file shape is inferred (`BLK-0015`).
5. `app.review` has no observed normal-route writer, and assessment creation is
   transfer-owned in the current static inventory. Literal absence is not
   treated as deletion or dormancy proof (`BLK-0016`).
6. `app.token_use` can be rebuilt at runtime with a different column ordinal,
   and its nullable `has_failed_requests` is coerced by the TypeScript record
   mapper. The authoritative null/ordinal/version contract is unresolved
   (`BLK-0017`).

### US-005 Unavailable Runtime Evidence

Applied migration names, deployed DuckDB/SQLite fields and ordinals, implicit
SQLite catalog contents, file/WAL bytes, row counts, sequence high-water marks,
null ratios, JSON key frequencies, duplicate generations, oldest/newest
timestamps, retry/repair ages, optimizer plans, index use/cost, orphan evidence,
and retention/recovery horizons are unavailable. `BLK-0007` applies to the
DuckDB objects; `BLK-0015` applies to local files. No live DuckDB or SQLite file,
server, worker, migration, repair, benchmark, fixture, or data writer was opened
or run, and no benchmark-critical value was defaulted.

## US-006 Judgment Job And Execution-Control Census

This story inventories judgment-job orchestration separately from the durable
judgment facts in US-005. It covers eight canonical DuckDB tables, five
application-declared per-job SQLite tables, the judge-worker
`accepted_claim` table, 16 current named indexes, the per-job lease JSON file,
and the judge-worker lock JSON file. It cross-references rather than duplicates
US-005's execution snapshot (`DBO-0038`), outbox-import marker
(`DBO-0039`), local outboxes/pending token use (`DBO-0040`-`DBO-0042`),
implicit SQLite sequence (`DBO-0043`), their indexes
(`DBO-0047`-`DBO-0059`), and both SQLite file containers
(`DBO-0060`-`DBO-0061`).

The DuckDB shape below applies every checked-in migration in the runner's
full-file-name lexical order. The SQLite shape combines each base `CREATE`
with every runtime add-column, rename/backfill, repair, and index helper.
Neither source derivation is deployed-shape proof: no live DuckDB or local
SQLite file was opened. All US-006 storage dispositions remain `unresolved`;
`recommendationActionability` remains `unresolved`,
`overallCertification` remains `INCOMPLETE`, and no recommendation,
target-shape, retention, or implementation row is added.

three maintenance freshness/recovery indexes; two provider lease
kind/request indexes; two request-closeout token/provider-attempt indexes; one

two accepted-claim accepted-order indexes. Dropped 0060 provider expiry, 0046
health freshness, and legacy queue status/created indexes are not counted.

### Lifecycle, Payload, And Environment Boundaries

| Control family | Source-observed create/update/terminal lifecycle | Persisted payload/state boundary | Production versus non-production evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Job/import/storage | Route inserts `not_started`; persisted status writers use `not_started`, `waiting_on_llm_connection`, `waiting_on_db_connection`, `running`, `paused`, `failed`, `completed`, and `project_removed`; they also update pause/import timestamps/errors/counts, cursor, tuning, and `active`, `draining`, `drained`, or `quarantined` storage before cleanup/delete | SQL does not constrain the status/storage vocabularies or one-job-per-project; `error` is JSON and open at SQL | Routes, cron, import, repair, startup, archive cleanup are production; route/service tests are corroboration only |
| Maintenance/health | Work leases claim/start/progress/fail/retry/fresh/complete; health snapshots publish with projected/fresh timestamps, local queue/outbox/ack counts and byte metrics, then expire/delete | Only maintenance scope kind is DB-enumerated; work/recovery/role types are TypeScript-only. Health rows are overwrite projections and have no final named index | Lease/health services and routes are production; focused tests/types do not prove deployed freshness or file bytes |
| Provider admission | Request or probe lease acquire, heartbeat, expire/reconcile, release | Compound semantics are encoded in one checked `lease_identity`; no FK binds request attempt/provider/endpoint and no history is retained after release | Admission service/internal route/telemetry are production; fencing tests are non-production |

| Telemetry/delete recovery | Sampler inserts per job/provider/time, history route buckets/reads and prunes after three days; delete service marks pending, increments attempts/errors, retries at startup, clears on success | Relational summary has checks; full telemetry remains JSON. Three-day pruning is code policy, not a DB constraint. Delete-pending has no retry/status check | Sampler/history/delete/startup are production; history/delete/route tests are non-production |
| Per-job SQLite | Initialize immutable-ish job info; scan cursor/epoch/acks; queue ready/claim/run/retry/judge/skip; heartbeat upsert/prune; completion ack insert/repair; retention/repair/delete operate on terminal state | No FKs or status checks. Model/provider JSON repeats US-004 open domains. Queue and ack request manifests copy US-005 attempt evidence. Runtime upgrades and repairs existing files without a ledger | SQLite service/import/worker flows are production; disposable tests are schema/lifecycle corroboration only |
| Worker accepted claim | Insert accepted payload before remote work; CAS/repair request manifest; replay into completion/pending-token handoff; rollout cleanup removes safe terminal claims | Payload names prompt/job/model/content/snapshot identity but nested prompt/snapshot/provider values remain open; relational columns are not SQL-checked against payload | Worker journal and owner-handoff flows are production; journal/persistence tests are non-production |

The 27 US-006 path-family rows are `CMF-0635`-`CMF-0661`. They
name: job-error array values; maintenance recovery context; request-closeout
durable-reference keys; telemetry root, dispatch, request/waiter, source,
coverage, provider, convergence, lease-authority, endpoint, and target-allocation

Ten new path-family rows remain `blocked`: arbitrary maintenance recovery
context, unknown closeout spread keys, dynamic telemetry endpoint-map keys,
copied open model/provider config, queue/completion/accepted provider
diagnostics, open nested accepted payload values, and legacy keys preserved by
job-lease heartbeat. A runtime profile would not turn these open contracts into
closed schemas. `BLK-0023` and `OQ-0028` retain that owner decision.

## US-007 Census Deltas, Outboxes, And Reusable Hot Facts

This story inventories the two durable review-serving intake ledgers, their
source-change recovery outbox, the source-partition high-water allocator, and
the typed import hot-fact table introduced by migration 0097. It adds five
DuckDB tables, nine current named indexes, 96 physical columns, and seven JSON
key/path-family rows. The effective shape applies the full checked-in migration
list in lexical file-name order; no later migration alters or drops these five
tables or nine indexes.

The similarly named `app.review_project_import_delta_cursor` is discovered but
not duplicated here: US-008 explicitly owns project-import cursors, dirty work,
acknowledgments, and projector watermarks. Likewise, generated temporary tables
`review_selected_import_serving_rebuild_v4` and
`review_selected_import_serving_update_v4` are recorded as hidden SQL
references, while their object/field census remains with US-014's temporary
shape inventory. All US-007 storage dispositions remain `unresolved`;
`recommendationActionability` remains `unresolved`, `overallCertification`
remains `INCOMPLETE`, and no schema, route, projector, retention, runtime, or
data change is proposed or performed.

### Dynamic SQL, Allowlists, Generated Names, And Repeated Extraction

1. `ReviewServingDeltaTable` is a two-literal allowlist used by a generated
   `FROM ${table}` duplicate lookup. Separately,
   `getDeltaIntakePartitions(database, tableName: string)` interpolates a plain
   string; its current call closure supplies only the same two literals.
2. `reviewServingChangeKinds` and `reviewServingInvalidationRegistry` jointly
   govern the 14 accepted change kinds, required keys, first component,
   dependents, and update mode. `reviewImportHotFieldProjectorColumns` is the
   registry that drives hot-field intake/projector column sets.
3. `ReviewServingProjectorWritableTable`,
   `reviewServingRegisteredSqlTables`, and `cleanupTableSpecs` omit the five
   US-007 objects. That explains why generic writer/read/retention searches do
   not enumerate them; direct services own the observed writes/reads, while
   retention remains unowned.
4. Selected-import SQL generates
   `review_selected_import_serving_rebuild_v4` and
   `review_selected_import_serving_update_v4`. US-014 owns their eventual
   temporary-shape rows.
5. Current-link and transfer writers repeatedly extract typed hot values from
   `import_metadata` aliases `articleTitle|title`,
   `journalTitle|journal|journalName`, `publicationYear|year`, Covidence
   conflict/duplicate flags, and `match_metadata.duplicateKey`. These source
   JSON paths already have immutable US-003 rows and are not duplicated.
6. Full selected-import, dirty selected-import, and display-payload SQL still
   extract `$.covidence.citation.url` directly from `raw_payload`; that path is
   already `CMF-0139`/`CMF-0149`. URL is not a hot-field column, so the repeated
   extraction and intended typed-fact boundary remain unresolved.

### Current Gaps And Unavailable Runtime Evidence

1. Static production call closure finds no caller for outbox append or per-row
   reconciliation, no lease claim/update, and no cursor reconciliation-state
   writer. The code and tests prove callable mechanics, not an operating
   producer/drainer/replay loop (`BLK-0024`).
2. Delta and recovery serializers accept generic identity values and spreads;
   the repository has no versioned closed schemas or immutable deployed key
   profile for unexpected/replayed values (`BLK-0025`).
3. The typed hot table deliberately reuses source JSON, but several persisted
   provenance fields are writer-only in current source and URL remains raw-JSON
   extraction in three projector paths. Authority, backfill, retention, and
   typed/raw equivalence remain owner questions (`BLK-0026`).
4. `app.review_project_import_delta_cursor` and its index are deferred to
   US-008, and the two generated temp tables to US-014; discovery here must not
   be read as absence or final classification.

## US-008 Census Dirty Work, Acknowledgements, And Watermarks

This story inventories four DuckDB control tables, three current named
indexes, and the persisted projection-input watermark subshape on
`app.review_projection_identity_manifest`. It adds eight schema-object rows,
57 physical-field rows, and five serialized JSON/path-family rows. The complete
migration list was applied conceptually in full-file-name lexical order; no
live DuckDB was opened. Migration 0115 is the final declaration of the
projector-watermark table, and migration 0116 makes its intended current index
count zero.

US-009 owns the remaining fields and publication lifecycle of
`app.review_projection_identity_manifest`; US-008 records only its scalar and
per-source input watermarks and does not allocate a duplicate table row.
Likewise, the three startup-probe temporary names discovered through the repair
registry remain assigned to US-014's temporary-shape census. Every US-008
storage disposition and `recommendationActionability` remains `unresolved`,
and `overallCertification` remains `INCOMPLETE`.

| Dirty work | Delta intake and `repairDirtyWork` call the dedicated service; deterministic ID hashes component/identity plus dirty scope. A conflict widens watermarks/ranges, replaces latest delta, resets `pending`, and refreshes `updated_at`. | Worker claims one component/projection/partition lane by atomically changing eligible `pending`, stale `running`, or stale `failed` rows to `running`; release/fail/complete write `pending`/`failed`/`completed`. Diagnostics and rebuild bootstrap read queue state. | There is no persisted claim owner, lease expiry, attempt count, error, or completion timestamp. A 15-minute `updated_at` timeout is the only stale-claim signal, and no delete/retention path is wired (`BLK-0027`). |
| Acknowledgements | Completion inserts deterministic point acknowledgements before marking dirty work complete. The callable compactor inserts a deterministic high-water row with `dirty_work_id NULL`, advances it with `GREATEST`, and deletes covered point rows. | Dirty upsert checks completed component/identity/partition high-water and enclosing ranges to skip replay. Startup repair probes duplicate keys and mutation capability. | The compactor has no production caller; point/high-water retention, range semantics, completion/ack atomicity across all direct paths, and recovery from ownerless stale claims remain unowned (`BLK-0027`). |
| Project import cursor | Only migration/defaults create its key, status, counters, leases, errors, cursor and timestamps. No production owner was found. | Only a schema inventory test and historical plans reference it; the cursor payload has no serializer or reader. | Schema plus intended design is not an operating import recovery path. Reachability, JSON schema, transitions, lease fencing, cleanup, and disposition remain blocked (`BLK-0029`). |
| Projector watermark | Projector writer and the completion-and-advance helper assert the outbox barrier, update by deterministic ID, then insert when absent. Insert populates only identity/source high-water columns; other fields stay defaults/null. | Startup repair counts duplicates and probes writes. No product/diagnostic reader of the persisted row, no lease claimant, and no writer for generation/patch/snapshot/status/cursor/error fields was found. | Final storage has no DB uniqueness/index; the promise-map lock is process-local. Multi-process insert races, duplicate resolution, the 0115 `any_value` merge, field ownership, and retention/recovery are unresolved (`BLK-0028`). |
| Projection input watermarks | Claim-manifest seeding, projectors, selected-import full rebuild, and rebuild bootstrap write a scalar and stable-serialized map through the manifest repository. | Snapshot promotion and diagnostics check component-specific scalar and per-source freshness; worker/rebuild paths read manifests for candidate state and finalization. | Scalar/map coherence, dynamic key/version authority, duplicated promotion/diagnostic registries, upgrade-path null/default drift, and retention/publication lifecycle require US-009 ownership and deployed proof (`BLK-0030`). |

### Dynamic Registries, Serialized Keys, And Hidden References

1. `reviewServingProjectionComponents` defines 11 components. The worker's
   `defaultComponentOrder` and `getDefaultReviewServingProjectorRunners` provide
   the production claim/run ownership map for the same 11 values; SQL does not
   constrain component strings.
2. `reviewServingInvalidationRegistry` maps all 14 declared change kinds to
   required keys, update mode, first affected component, downstream topology,
   and dirty-work fan-out. Delta intake is the active writer path; a registry
   declaration is not a lifecycle or retention owner.
3. `projection_key` is stable serialized JSON with exactly
   `{projectionComponent,projectionIdentity}` at the current serializer
   boundary. Dirty scope identity separately hashes dirty kind, project, scope,
   source partition, and optional projection key; those values are relational
   fields rather than a second persisted JSON object.
4. `sourcePartitionAliases` emits the observed source prefix and, when known,
   one of `reviewChange`, `importRunArticle`, or `projectScope`. Named prefixes
   include `article`, `humanJudgment`, `llmJudgment`, `promptConfig`,
   `projectReviewConfig`, `review-change`, `import-run-article`, `importRoute`,
   `project-scope`, and `projectScope`; the `Record<string, number>` type still
   permits additional source-prefix keys.
5. Promotion and diagnostics each maintain a separate
   `componentSourceWatermarkKeys` registry over review-change,
   import-run-article, and project-scope aliases. They also accept a
   component-name override from snapshot source watermarks. Source code proves
   current named keys, not registry synchronization or a closed deployed map.
6. `duckdbStartupIndexedTableRepairSpecs` names fixed temporary tables
   `startup_probe_review_serving_dirty_work`,
   `startup_probe_review_serving_dirty_work_ack`, and
   `startup_probe_review_serving_projector_watermark`. Their eventual temporary
   field census remains US-014 scope; the registry is recorded here because it
   is an initial production reader/writer missed by ordinary service searches.
7. `ReviewServingProjectorWritableTable` and retention `cleanupTableSpecs` omit
   all four control tables. Direct services explain active dirty/ack/watermark
   writes; there is no equivalent production service for the project-import
   cursor and no observed cleanup for any of them.

The five serialized path-family rows are `CMF-0781`, `CMF-0804`,
`CMF-0822`, and `CMF-0825`-`CMF-0826`. The projection-key and named watermark
rows are finite at current writer boundaries. Project-import cursor JSON,
projector cursor JSON, and additional dynamic input-watermark keys remain
`blocked`; no keys or values are invented from resolver defaults.

### Current Gaps And Unavailable Runtime Evidence

1. Dirty work has an active producer/consumer loop but no durable owner/fence,
   acknowledgement compaction schedule, or retention/delete path
   (`BLK-0027`).
2. The final projector watermark deliberately lacks a primary key and named
   index; static code supplies only process-local serialization and no reader
   for most persisted control fields (`BLK-0028`).
3. The project-import cursor remains schema/test/plan-only and its JSON,
   transition, lease, recovery, and cleanup contracts are unavailable
   (`BLK-0029`).
4. Projection input maps have a dynamic key domain, duplicated requirement
   registries, and clean-install versus upgrade-path constraint drift
   (`BLK-0030`).

rows. The two physical input-watermark fields on
`app.review_projection_identity_manifest` remain counted only once under
`DBO-0112`/`CMF-0823`-`CMF-0824`; US-009 cross-references them while owning the

migration runner's full-file-name lexical order. Migration 0097 declares all
five tables and indexes; 0103 only performs the already-recorded conditional
input-map add/backfill, and no later migration through 0117 changes the US-009
objects. No live DuckDB was opened. Every disposition and
`recommendationActionability` remains `unresolved`, and
`overallCertification` remains `INCOMPLETE`.

| Projection publication | Manifest `created_at`, `updated_at`, mutable `status` | Projectors/rebuild seed insert or update candidate manifests | No `published_at`, `activated_at`, `retired_at`, owner, or production non-candidate transition; update time conflates all mutations (`BLK-0031`). |
| Selected-import build publication | Header `started_at`, `completed_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`; base `selected_import_updated_at` | Writer sets start on first insert and completion only when the batch reports completed; rebuild reset deletes and recreates | `owner`, lease, failure timestamp, retry/retirement time, completed-header/base referential fence, and header cleanup owner are absent or inactive (`BLK-0033`). |
| Candidate snapshot | Manifest `created_at`, `updated_at`; nullable validation/failure state | Bootstrap creates/upserts candidate; worker refreshes component state | Candidate upsert clears failure fields but not `activated_at`; invalid promotion returns an error without persisting failed state. Reused deterministic IDs can therefore retain lifecycle ambiguity (`BLK-0031`). |
| Active publication | `snapshot_status='active'`, `activated_at`, `updated_at` | Transactional projector promotion after selected snapshot and component validation | No actor/owner or single-active SQL constraint; `reviewConfigHash` null-safe grouping is application-only (`BLK-0031`). |
| Last-known-good | New active row stores prior active snapshot ID; readers fall back to that ID or the latest retired row ordered by activation/update | Promotion and manifest readers; route/read services consume it | No FK/status/config constraint or dedicated assignment time/owner; direct pointer read does not require the target to remain retired/active (`BLK-0031`). |
| Retirement | Prior active row changes to retired and only `updated_at` changes; test-only helper can retire other non-active rows | Production promotion retires prior active; generic retire helper has no non-test caller | No `retired_at`, reason, actor, generation, or immutable publication history. `activated_at` is retained and `updated_at` cannot distinguish retirement from other writes (`BLK-0031`). |
| Pin acquisition/protection | `created_at`, `updated_at`, `expires_at`, nullable `released_at`, owner kind/ID, ref count | Bulk operation creation acquires/increments a deterministic pin; active predicates require unreleased, positive ref count, future expiry | No production caller of the standalone increment/release/expire helpers, terminal-job hook, orphan sweep, or row deletion. Pin acquisition and job insert are separate calls (`BLK-0034`). |
| Failed publication | Snapshot `failed_at`, `last_error`; selected snapshot `last_error` | Exported failed-marker exists only in tests; startup repair temporarily mutates/restores candidate snapshot rows | No normal invalid-promotion failure transition; selected snapshot only clears `last_error`, and projection manifests have no failure owner (`BLK-0031`, `BLK-0033`). |

### Persisted JSON Key And Open-Domain Census

1. Selected-import cursor serialization names exactly `articleId`,
   `processedRowCount`, `rankKeySort`, and `rankNumericSort`. The validator
   checks those keys but does not reject extras; an empty terminal batch can
   reserialize an existing object unchanged, so additional keys remain open.
2. Current production `composed_identity_json` names `componentSet`,
   `requestKind`, `reviewConfigHash`, and `selectedImportSnapshotId` for V4
   bootstrap. The repository and pin serializer accept recursive
   `ReviewServingIdentityValue`, so both manifest and copied pin domains remain
   open beyond those observed keys.
3. `component_state_json` has root keys `required` and `optional`; every entry
   has `baseGeneration`, `component`, `patchWatermark`, `projectionIdentity`,
   and `requirement`. `required_components_json` and
   `optional_components_json` are arrays over the 11 source-defined component
   strings. SQL does not validate keys, membership, uniqueness, ordering, or
   agreement across the three columns.
4. `source_watermarks_json` currently receives the named source prefixes and
   aliases already recorded in `CMF-0825`; promotion also accepts any of the 11
   component names as override keys. The serializer type and source-partition
   prefixing remain recursively/dynamically open.
5. Successful or failed validation writes exactly `error`, `ok`,
   `requiredComponentCount`, and `snapshotId`. Candidate creation accepts a
   broader identity value, so additional root/nested keys remain an open
   domain even though the current promotion builder is finite.

The 14 JSON/path-family rows are `CMF-0901`-`CMF-0914`. Five additional/open
domains (`CMF-0902`, `CMF-0904`, `CMF-0910`, `CMF-0912`, and `CMF-0914`)
remain `blocked`; source code names current keys but no versioned closed schema
or approved immutable non-live profile permits invented closure.

### Current Gaps And Unavailable Runtime Evidence

1. Projection manifest, component-state, serving snapshot, composed identity,
   and pin identity are distinct contracts. Current dirty identity omits
   definition/config/generation/watermark state, manifests mutate in place,
   and snapshot publication does not transition projection manifests
   (`BLK-0031`).
2. Manifest composed identity, snapshot source watermarks, validation values,
   copied pin identity, and selected cursor accept open keys or recursive
   values without a versioned SQL/runtime schema (`BLK-0032`).
3. Selected snapshot owner/lease/error fields do not form an active claim
   lifecycle; base/header FKs, retirement, orphan cleanup, and retention
   equivalence are missing (`BLK-0033`).
4. Pins have an active acquisition/protection path but no production release,
   expiry, terminal-job hook, orphan cleanup, or row-retention owner
   (`BLK-0034`).

Applied migration names, deployed constraints/defaults/indexes, duplicate or
orphan identities, status/config distributions, generation/watermark drift,
component-map disagreement, candidate/active/retired/failure ages, selected
cursor/base counts, pin owner/ref/expiry/release state, startup-repair history,
physical bytes, optimizer plans/use, and cleanup horizons remain unavailable.
`BLK-0007`, `BLK-0030`, and `BLK-0031`-`BLK-0034` apply. No live DuckDB,
server, worker, projector, migration, repair, benchmark, or data operation ran.

## US-010 Census Rebuilds, Overlays, Jobs, And Retention

This story inventories six DuckDB control tables, six current named indexes,
and one logical persisted bulk-result-manifest subshape. It adds 13
schema-object rows, 141 physical-field rows, and 28 serialized JSON/path-family
rows. No row from US-003 through US-009 is duplicated.

The complete checked-in migration list was applied conceptually in the
migration runner's full-file-name lexical order. Migration 0097 declares the
chunk, overlay, bulk-job, search-job, and retention-mark tables plus four
indexes. Migration 0102 is a clean-install no-op for the already-present
overlay read-surface column but can leave a legacy upgraded column nullable
with a default. Migration 0107 creates rebuild requests, adds 32 chunk fields,
and adds two indexes; 0109 performs targeted request/chunk recovery without
changing their shapes; and 0111 is the final request-table rebuild and index
declaration. No later migration through 0117 changes these objects. No live
DuckDB was opened.

Every storage disposition and `recommendationActionability` remains
`unresolved`. The source-observed status, admission, retry, lease, reconciliation,
result, and cleanup values below are storage contracts; none is substituted for
the US-001 manifest `auditStatus` vocabulary.

retention cursor key.

Thirteen additional/open domains (`CMF-1058`, `CMF-1060`, `CMF-1062`,
`CMF-1065`, `CMF-1067`, `CMF-1069`, `CMF-1071`, `CMF-1073`,
`CMF-1075`-`CMF-1078`, and `CMF-1081`) remain `blocked`. Generic recursive

### US-010 Static Findings And Limits

1. Request-level and chunk-level lease/retry contracts are not equivalent.
   Chunk claims persist and fence an owner/expiry; request lease fields are
   clear-only and request retry fields do not operate as a parallel scheduler
   (`BLK-0036`, `BLK-0037`).
2. Bulk job freshness is not a durable lease. A stale `updated_at` row can be
   reclaimed, but no owner/token is persisted and progress/terminal writes are
   not fenced to the claimant. Terminal jobs also retain their separately
   acquired snapshot pins (`BLK-0039`, `BLK-0034`).
3. Async substring search has a durable request row but no operating recovery
   path. The synthetic interruption registry and passing insertion/contract
   tests do not supply an executor (`BLK-0040`).
4. Overlay TTL and retention cutoffs are not cleanup proof. Active overlay reads
   enforce time, while no production reconcile/expire sweep exists; retention
   advances an 11-table cursor but does not use its cutoff values or include any
   US-010 control table (`BLK-0038`, `BLK-0041`).
5. Request/chunk startup repair and 0109 recovery are narrow. They do not close
   parent/request/snapshot/job/pin FKs, dangling children, abandoned pins,
   terminal-row horizons, or general orphan cleanup (`BLK-0035`-`BLK-0041`).

Applied/deployed field/index existence, row/byte counts, null and distinct
profiles, status/retry/lease/result distributions, stale/expired ages,
parent/request/snapshot/pin/orphan counts, claim races, index plans/use,
recovery history, cleanup lag, JSON key frequencies, and retention horizons
remain unavailable. `BLK-0007`, `BLK-0034`, and `BLK-0035`-`BLK-0042` apply.
No live DuckDB, server, worker, projector, migration, repair, benchmark, or
production data operation ran; focused tests used mocks/source reads and
disposable `/tmp` fixtures only.

## US-011 Census Candidate, Display, And Status Marts

This story inventories five DuckDB mart tables and six current named indexes.
It adds 11 schema-object rows and 111 current-forward physical-field rows: 44
candidate-serving fields, 24 display-patch fields, 17 selected-import-patch
fields, 14 LLM-status fields, and 12 human-status fields. None of the five
current-forward declarations has a JSON column, so this slice adds zero JSON
key/path-family rows. The LLM table's
`answered_original_as_array VARCHAR[]` is a typed DuckDB array column, not a
persisted JSON object, and is counted once as a physical field.

The complete checked-in migration list was applied conceptually in the
migration runner's full-file-name lexical order. Current 0097 clean-install DDL
already contains all five final table shapes and six indexes. The two 0104
migrations and 0105 idempotently add nullable candidate/display metadata fields
for older paths; 0106 is a marker-only `SELECT`; and 0108 idempotently adds four
nullable selected-import display fields and backfills qualifying legacy patch
rows. No later migration through 0117 changes these objects or indexes. No live
DuckDB was opened. Historical plan evidence records that already-applied local
databases may still retain an unused `source_metadata JSON` column on candidate
serving and display patch because 0106 could not drop it in place; that
deployed-only possibility is not counted as current forward DDL and remains
blocked under `BLK-0043`.

Every storage disposition and `recommendationActionability` remains
`unresolved`. Object names, index names, inherited prose, direct row consumers,
and writer function names are not accepted as column-level pre-limit or
post-limit proof. Accordingly, every `CMF-1084`-`CMF-1194` row records both use
columns as `unknown` until a later `MAP-####`/`LIN-####` story proves exact SQL
placement and boundedness.

## US-012 Census Payload, Search, And Queue Marts

This story inventories five DuckDB mart tables and six current named indexes.
It adds 11 schema-object rows and 69 material-field rows: 55 physical columns
plus 14 persisted JSON key/path-family rows. The physical fields comprise 11
article-payload fields, 15 judgment-detail fields, 9 title-search fields, 10
queue-patch fields, and 10 unassessed-queue fields. Three copied JSON domains
remain open and are added as blocked manifest rows; no finite keys are invented
for them.

The complete checked-in migration list was applied conceptually in the
migration runner's full-file-name lexical order. Current 0097 clean-install DDL
declares all five objects and all six indexes. Migration 0098 repeats the
article-payload `article_created_at` addition and preview-order index for older
paths; 0099 rebuilds judgment detail to the current option-table-era shape;
0103 rebuilds the unassessed queue with `queue_identity` in its primary key and
index; and 0109 performs the final judgment-detail payload-kind rebuild plus a
targeted rebuild-request/chunk recovery update. No later migration through 0117
changes these objects or indexes. No migration or live DuckDB operation ran.

Every storage disposition and `recommendationActionability` remains
`unresolved`. Object names, read-contract strategy labels, index expressions,
current consumers, and writer formulas are declarations or reachability
evidence, not necessity proof. Accordingly, every `CMF-1195`-`CMF-1263` row
records candidate, hydration, priority, and search necessity as `unknown` until
an adopted `MAP-####`/`LIN-####` row proves exact statement placement,
boundedness, and consumers.

### Candidate, Hydration, Priority, And Search Boundary

All 69 new field-manifest rows deliberately use `Pre-limit use` to preserve
candidate, priority, and search necessity as `unknown`, and `Post-limit use` to
preserve hydration necessity as `unknown`. Current SQL shows that some values
are written, joined, filtered, ordered, or returned, but US-012 does not yet
adopt a complete route-to-query boundary for every mounted/browser/desktop,
bulk, export and job path. The field rows therefore do not turn observed use
into a necessity classification or a resolved disposition.

`BLK-0048` and `OQ-0053` own the later exact proof: statement boundaries,
predicate/order/cursor placement, `LIMIT`, article-set size/byte caps, queue
priority semantics, token-search behavior, output consumers, negative paths,
and approved optimizer plans.

### US-012 Static Findings And Limits

1. `projectReviewServingQueuePatches` is an operation name, not evidence that
   `mart.review_queue_patch_v4` participates. Current source directly replaces
   unassessed-serving rows; the physical patch literal is migration/test-only
   and absent from writer/startup/retention registries (`BLK-0050`).
2. Current 0097 is clean-install-complete, but 0098, 0099, 0103 and 0109 remain
   material forward paths. In particular, 0103 destructively rebuilds the
   queue without a data copy, and 0109 combines schema repair with narrow
   rebuild-state recovery; static source does not prove deployed completion
   (`BLK-0047`).
3. The article payload duplicates open metadata keys through a merge, while the
   judgment payload constructs a closed outer envelope around open model and
   quote values. Current serializers cannot convert those three copied domains
   into finite schemas (`BLK-0049`).
4. Keys constrain stored row identity but not semantic equality: payload and
   component IDs lack FKs/coherence checks, judgment JSON is not constrained to
   relational fields, search has no tokenizer-version constraint, and queue
   kind/priority/identity/null behavior is not SQL-domain constrained
   (`BLK-0051`).

completion, row/byte/token/prompt fan-out, JSON key/value frequency, null and
domain distributions, physical widths, update ages, duplicate/orphan state,
per-field four-axis lineage, optimizer plans, index use/selectivity/size/write
cost, startup-repair history, cleanup lag and retention horizons remain
unavailable. `BLK-0047`-`BLK-0051` apply. No live DuckDB, server, worker,
projector, migration, repair, benchmark, retention-worker, or production data
operation ran.


## US-013 Census Postings, Summaries, Filters, And Partial Marts

This story inventories nine DuckDB mart tables and eight current named
indexes. It adds 17 schema-object rows and 123 material-field rows: 115
physical columns plus eight persisted JSON/text-encoded key/path-family rows.
The physical fields comprise 11 posting-patch fields, 10 posting-serving
fields, 10 posting-stat fields, 9 persistent-contribution fields, 12 count
fields, 14 facet fields, 16 filter-option fields, 22 summary-partial fields,
and 11 contribution-partial fields. All current serializer envelopes in this
slice are finite, so US-013 adds no blocked open-domain row.

The complete checked-in migration list was applied conceptually in the
migration runner's full-file-name lexical order. Migration 0097 declares the
posting, posting-stat, persistent-contribution, count, facet, and filter-option
families. Migration 0099 destructively rebuilds count and repeats the option
declaration; 0100 destructively rebuilds filter options; 0101 destructively
rebuilds facets; 0112 and 0113 add the two request-scoped partial tables; and
0114 drops both qualified and unqualified spellings of the posting-stat lookup
index. No later migration through 0117 changes any US-013 object. No migration
or live DuckDB operation ran.

Roles are recorded independently of disposition. Posting serving, posting
stats, counts, facets, and filter options are active serving/derived-serving
storage. The posting patch is a staging declaration with no exact current
production owner. The persistent summary-contribution table likewise has no
exact current production owner and is only marked potentially retired.
The two rebuild-partial tables are active request/chunk-scoped staging and
reduction state. Every storage disposition and
`recommendationActionability` remains `unresolved`.

### US-013 Static Findings And Limits

1. Current posting work directly mutates serving/stats, and current summary
   work computes contributions in memory or writes request-scoped partials.
   The physical posting patch and persistent contribution tables have no exact
   non-migration production literal. Negative tests and retention labels
   establish current bypass, not deployed absence, safe deletion or historical
   compatibility (`BLK-0053`, `BLK-0054`).
2. Summary-partial reduction deletes completed source summary-partial batches
   after accumulating them. It leaves the accumulator row, never deletes
   contribution-partial rows, and neither partial table is in startup repair or
   retention. Successful finalization therefore does not prove cleanup for
   completed, failed, abandoned or orphaned requests (`BLK-0055`).
3. Count, facet and option shapes are exact source declarations, but 0099,
   0100 and 0101 rebuild their tables without row copies, while 0114 removes
   the posting-stat named index. Static source cannot prove all deployed
   databases completed those transitions and regenerated equivalent rows
   (`BLK-0052`).
4. Current option SQL retains `answer_id` and both numeric bound columns as
   null. That is a source-observed writer fact, not proof that the columns are
   unnecessary across deployed, operator, import/export or future-compatible
   paths (`BLK-0056`).
5. PKs constrain physical identity but not posting/filter/summary value
   grammars, stable-text equality, component/snapshot FKs, count/selectivity
   arithmetic, availability/value/stale coherence, option-payload equality or
   partial/request terminal state (`BLK-0056`).

Applied/deployed field and index existence, migration ledger and rebuild
completion, row/byte/posting/value/prompt/chunk fan-out, duplicate-byte cost,
null/domain distributions, exact summary parity, stale ages, duplicate/orphan
state, per-field route/query/limit lineage, optimizer plans, index
use/selectivity/size/write cost, startup-repair history, partial cleanup lag,
and retention horizons remain unavailable. `BLK-0052`-`BLK-0056` apply.
No live DuckDB, server, worker, projector, migration, repair, benchmark,
retention-worker or production data operation ran.


## US-014 Census Legacy, Temporary, Payload, And Local-File Shapes

US-014 closes the source-defined storage discovery pass before API-to-storage
lineage. It conceptually applies every checked-in DuckDB migration in complete
file-name lexical order and never opens, queries, copies, or infers from the
live DuckDB. The remaining permanent surface is 41 tables with 553 physical
fields and 40 current named indexes. Temporary storage is counted separately:
105 literal migration declarations in 18 migration families and 51 production
runtime `CREATE TEMP TABLE` sites in 13 naming/lifecycle families. The latter
include 20 fixed startup-probe names plus one generated indexed-table probe
pattern; declaration-site count is not a claim about simultaneous tables.

The file census adds 32 path/artifact families. Existing per-job SQLite,
worker-journal, job-lease and journal-lock containers remain `DBO-0060`,
`DBO-0061`, `DBO-0092` and `DBO-0093`; existing article full-text columns and
payload domains remain `DBO-0001`, `CMF-0039`-`CMF-0051` and
`CMF-0114`-`CMF-0118`. US-014 cross-references those immutable rows instead of
double-counting them. No adjacent shape is marked `out-of-scope`, and no
storage disposition is resolved.

### Runtime Root And File Lifecycle Census

`runtimeWritablePath.ts` makes a relative path mean `<cwd>/<path>` in the
normal browser/server flow and `<dirname(DUCKDB_PATH)>/<path>` in desktop mode;
`:memory:` falls back to cwd. Desktop's default root is
`~/Library/Application Support/Forska/desktop` on macOS,
`%LOCALAPPDATA%/Forska/desktop` on Windows, and
`${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/forska/desktop` on Linux. The normal default
database instead ends at `Forska/forska.duckdb` (macOS/Windows) or
`forska/forska.duckdb` (Linux), and an explicit relative `DUCKDB_PATH` resolves
against cwd. These roots are deployment schemes, not proof that any file
exists.

| DBO row | Exact path/file scheme | Owner, producer and consumer | Lifecycle, retention, recovery and browser/desktop implication |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DBO-0291` | configured/default `forska.duckdb` or `:memory:` | DuckDB service/migrations own; all app persistence consumers depend on it | Checkpoint/close/owner recovery exist; physical bytes, deployed shape and backup policy blocked. Desktop rebases under data root. |
| `DBO-0292` | `${databasePath}.wal` | DuckDB engine writes; startup recovery, snapshot and backup helpers consume | Checkpoint/replay/quarantine paths exist; safe replay/deletion and deployed presence blocked. |
| `DBO-0293` | `DUCKDB_TEMP_DIRECTORY` or `${databasePath}.tmp` spill/temp path | DuckDB runner/engine owns; cleanup helper recognizes sibling temp path | No complete quota, retention, crash cleanup or desktop disk-pressure proof. |

### Payload And Browser/Desktop Boundaries

- The actual serializer boundary, not the broad TypeScript type, supplies every
  `CMF-1940`-`CMF-1982` named key. `unknown`, dynamic maps, provider metric
  values, copied metadata/quotes, log attributes, transfer warning values and
  transfer dependency-resolution values remain blocked open domains.
- `full_text` and `full_text_html` are DuckDB values, not inferred files.
  `full_text_pdf` and `full_text_assets` may point into `assets/`; their existing
  material rows remain authoritative. A persisted string is not file-existence,
  reachability, retention, or cleanup proof.
- Normal browser and desktop UI code share API paths. Desktop patches `fetch`
  through the local bridge and rebases runtime files under its data root;
  therefore a browser-only route test cannot prove desktop filesystem or
  download behavior. Streamed CSV/JSON outputs do not become server-retained
  files merely because the browser creates a Blob.
- No approved immutable local-file inventory, deployed migration ledger,
  physical size profile, filesystem permissions snapshot or browser/desktop
  parity capture exists. `BLK-0057`-`BLK-0064` preserve those limits, and all
  recommendations/dispositions stay `unresolved`.

## US-015 Approved Physical Baseline

US-015 is the first story that permits isolated disposable-fixture mutation,
but only after the fixture and every benchmark-critical setting are approved.
That approval gate did not pass. Repository source fixes the release-scale
shape and workload, but neither the task input nor an immutable repository
record supplies an approved fixture instance, generator/seed, model, provider,
thinking identity, prompt identities, content flags, explicit memory/runtime
settings, or physical snapshot identities. The repository also has no runnable
physical collector that emits the complete required table, byte, rebuild,
memory, and timing evidence.

No physical run was attempted. This is a blocked baseline record, not a
zero-valued baseline: absent row, byte, time, RSS, or WAL observations are
`unavailable`, never `0`. No resolver default, smoke value, test fixture, live
project, or existing database was substituted. `overallCertification` remains
`INCOMPLETE`, and no storage disposition or recommendation changes.

## US-016 LLM Review API And UI Surface Inventory

US-016 is a source-only inventory of the LLM review list route and the UI that
consumes it. Mounting is proven from actual plugin composition plus the public
route inventory; registry membership alone is not treated as reachability. The
route-inventory contract union is retained, but each contract below separately
states whether current production code invokes it, merely embeds its physical
table in another SQL statement, or only maps it to a route.

The SQL counts below are static successful-path counts of logical
`queryJson(...)` statements under local DuckDB ownership. They are not runtime
observations, optimizer work, network calls, or physical query measurements.
An owner-HTTP project-access read can replace the one local access statement.
Every accepted `readReviewServingRows` call contributes three logical
statements: one diagnostics bundle, one snapshot-manifest read, and one data
read. No live DuckDB, server, browser, desktop shell, or benchmark was opened.

### UI Response Consumption And Request Shape

- `API-0001` returns six envelope fields. `ReviewsArticlesTableContainer`
  consumes only `data` and `nextCursor`; `totalCount`, `page`, `limit`, and
  `totalPages` are ignored and a later `API-0002` result drives both displayed
  total and total pages.
- The count query consumes `totalCount` and `totalPages` but never rejects or
  renders the optional route `error`, so every caught server failure becomes a
  displayed zero. Its five-minute stale time is independent of the list query,
  which declares no stale time.
- The filter query returns only `response.filters` to the component. It uses
  `promptId`, `promptName`, `filterType`, enum `answeredOriginalValues`, and
  numeric `bins.{label,min,max}`/`specialValues`; it discards top-level
  `diagnostics`, `facets`, `filterOptions`, and `searchScope`.
- The LLM table consumes list-row `id`, `articleTitle`, `articleCreatedAt`,
  `articleUpdatedAt`, `articleId`, `arxivId`, `biorxivId`, `medrxivId`, `doi`,
  `pubmedId`, `journalTitle`, `url`, `originalData`, `sourceMetadata`,
  `fullTextPDF`, `fullTextFetchedAt`, `fullTextConversionStatus`,
  `judgments[].{promptId,answeredOriginal,answeredOriginalAsArray}`,
  `judgedPromptIds`, and `isFullyJudged`. It ignores returned
  `canonicalArticleId`, `selectedImportRouteId`, and judgment
  `id`, `createdAt`, article-copy fields, `modelId`, `explanation`, and
  `quotes`.
- `loadedPages` concatenates pages `1..currentPage`, so “Load more” grows the
  rendered table. Missing cursor state on a page above one resets to page one.
  Top and bottom `ReviewsPaginationControls` instances duplicate the same
  controls and each creates a `['projects-without-jobs']` observer plus bulk
  mutations; whether one network request is shared is runtime-unknown.
- `ReviewsProjectWarnings` and `ReviewsArticlesTableContainer` each create the
  same `['project-reviews-warnings', projectId]` observer. The latter admits
  list/count reads only when `indexing.serving.readable === true`. Same-key
  TanStack source composition is not a network-deduplication observation.
- URL state covers `from`, `to`, duplicate/conflict flags, `page`, `limit`,
  `search`, `llmStatus`, and dynamic `pf_<promptId>` values. LLM status defaults
  to `complete`; typed title text affects no query until form submission copies
  it to `appliedSearchTitle`.

All eight `UIR-####` rows are source-applicable to both normal browser and
desktop renderer flows. That applicability follows shared route/client code and
desktop origin/fetch bridging; neither runtime request counts nor semantic
parity were observed. `BLK-0068` and `BLK-0069` preserve those limits.

## US-017 Human Review API And UI Surface Inventory

US-017 is a source-only inventory of the Human review list/filter routes and
their UI consumers. Actual `ProjectsRoutes.ts` composition and the public route
inventory prove both mounts; the read-contract route inventory is retained as
a separate mapping source. Current production directly calls only the Human
row, Human judgment, Human facet and Human option contracts. Rows-by-set,
named count and standalone search contracts are mapped only, while posting and
title-search tables are embedded in row/direct-count SQL.

The SQL counts below are successful-first-attempt logical `queryJson(...)`
statement counts under local DuckDB ownership, not runtime observations,
network requests, optimizer work or physical measurements. Define
`C = ceil(R / max(1, min(100, floor(10000 / P))))` for `R` returned page rows
and maximum positive enabled-prompt count `P`; the service substitutes `P =
128` when no positive count exists. Define `K = 1` on a cold cached
`information_schema.columns` lookup for `app.project`, otherwise `K = 0`.
Last-known-good selection adds two manifest statements. Date and reader data
statements allow four underlying attempts with 100, 250 and 500 ms delays. The
dynamic count layers the same helper around that retrying database and can
therefore issue four outer groups of four attempts (16 underlying attempts) if
the matching transient error persists. Retry attempts are not included in the
successful-path formulas. No live DuckDB, server, browser, desktop shell or
benchmark was opened.
